idiom_name: package-level map + sync.RWMutex, filled from init()
implementation_notes: Go's registry is a package-level map guarded by a sync.RWMutex, populated from init() functions or explicit start-up wiring: the package itself is the well-known object, sql.Register/sql.Drivers in database/sql is the canonical standard-library instance of exactly this shape (a mutex-guarded map[string]driver.Driver, panic on duplicate registration, blank import to trigger init), and image.RegisterFormat and http.ServeMux follow the same idea at package or type scope. What replaces the classic Registry class is the map plus two functions; a struct with its own map and mutex (as in a ServeMux instance) is used only when several registries must coexist.
pitfalls: A plug-in only registers if its package is imported: forgetting the blank import (import _ "pkg") leaves the registry empty, and lookup fails at runtime with no compile-time signal (database/sql answers with 'unknown driver (forgotten import?)').
A plain map is not safe for concurrent use: two goroutines registering, or register and lookup overlapping, panic with 'concurrent map writes' - the mutex is not optional.
Package-level state makes tests order-dependent; provide an unexported reset (as database/sql does with unregisterAllDrivers) or a registry struct that tests can build fresh.
Registration from init() means the map is populated before main but in import-graph order, and any panic in init aborts the process.
